weakness.insightHeadline: You can look at the {label} area first.
weakness.insightDisclaimer: This is an estimate based on trends in your recent answers. Your actual weaknesses may shift with future practice.
weakness.insightWhyTitle: Why look at this area first?

grammar.why: When sentence rules waver, even good ideas can come across less precisely.
grammar.example: Tenses, particles, and connectors often get mixed up within an answer.
grammar.strategy: Rewrite in short sentences and try the same expression in a different tense.

vocab.why: A narrow word choice leads to repeating the same meaning, weakening your answer's persuasiveness.
vocab.example: You may repeat only easy words or pick expressions that fit the context less well.
vocab.strategy: While solving recommended problems, note two synonymous expressions each time.

structure.why: When structure falls apart, the link between claim and evidence becomes less clear to the reader.
structure.example: The order of intro, evidence, and conclusion may get swapped, or one paragraph may mix several ideas.
structure.strategy: Before writing, jot down one main claim and two supporting points.

content.why: Thin content leaves your claims unsupported, making it hard to earn points.
content.example: You may repeat the same point without examples or evidence.
content.strategy: In recommended problems, practice adding one example to each claim.

expression.why: Monotonous expression makes it hard to convey the same meaning in varied ways.
expression.example: You may repeat similar expressions or have awkward transitions.
expression.strategy: While solving recommended problems, write two alternative expressions each time.

topic_fit.why: Drifting off topic makes it hard to score, even if the sentences are correct.
topic_fit.example: Background explanation may run longer than what the prompt asked for.
topic_fit.strategy: Reread the prompt, check the required conditions, then trim your answer.

language.why: When language use wavers, meaning and tone can come across less precisely.
language.example: Awkward expressions or sentence links may repeat in context.
language.strategy: Reread your answer and check vocabulary, grammar, and sentence flow together.

fallback.why: This area scored low in your recent answers, so checking it first can help.
fallback.example: It's worth checking whether the same kind of mistake keeps recurring.
fallback.strategy: Solve recommended problems and revise your answer once more.

q51.titleHelp: Question 51 asks you to complete a short answer from the surrounding context.

q51.guidePlaceholder: Problem-specific guide content will appear here.
q51.tip0: Use an expression that explains the result of the issue stated earlier.
q51.tip1: Causal connectors such as therefore and for that reason are common here.
q51.tipsPlaceholder: Problem-specific writing tips will appear here.

q52.pageSubtitle: Check the conditions and write an answer that makes both blanks work as one flow.

q52.answerHintFallback: Connect the roles and conditions of both blanks into one coherent flow.
q52.answerPlaceholder: Write one answer for the two blanks.
q52.guideBody: Check the passage and conditions together, then make both blanks continue within the same topic flow.
q52.conditionFallback: Use the passage flow and blank markers to review the conditions for both blanks.
q52.guideFallback: Clarify the relationship between the surrounding sentences first, then connect both blanks as one natural answer.
q52.tip0: Check whether the first blank should receive a problem statement or definition from the previous sentence.
q52.tip1: The second blank should match the conclusion or example that follows.

q53.pageSubtitle: Use the graphs and conditions to compose a 200-300 character long-form answer.
q53.titleHelp: Question 53 asks you to analyze reference data and write a longer answer with intro, body, and conclusion.
q53.editorHint: Explain the key data changes with an intro, body, and conclusion structure.
q53.guideBody: Compare the materials first, then organize causes and results into one clear flow.

privacy.heading: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This page is a provisional notice on personal data handling for TALKPIK AI. The formal privacy policy will reflect compliance with Korea's Personal Information Protection Act and be published separately before launch.
privacy.summaryCollect: Data collected: email, name, learning activity logs, writing submissions, evaluation results.
privacy.summaryPurpose: Purpose of use: account identification, tracking learning progress, improving AI feedback quality.
privacy.summaryRetention: Retention period: destroyed immediately upon account withdrawal. Learning statistics may be retained in anonymized form after identifying information is removed.
privacy.summaryThirdParty: Third-party sharing: none. However, when an AI model is called, the body of a writing submission is transiently transmitted to an external LLM provider (the retention policy after the model responds is governed by the model provider's terms).
privacy.summaryScopeNote: The scope above is limited to processing as currently implemented. Until the formal review, we make no definitive retention-period commitments or new third-party sharing promises.
privacy.updateBody: When the formal privacy policy is published, this page will be updated, and the changes will be notified separately to registered users.
